To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sterol-sensings nuclear receptors liver X receptor (LXR) and LXR target gene, inducible degradator of the low density lipoprotein receptor (IDOL), promote ubiquitylation and degradation of a lipid-raft LDLR pool.
the LXR-IDL axis defines a clainrin-, caveolaa-, and dynaminindependent endocytic route of the LDLR that leads to lysosomal degradation.
the LXR-induced E3-ubiqutinylation enzyme IDOL promotes the internalization of a subset of LDL receptors into lipid rafts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of novel endocytic mechanisms.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie endocytic trafficking of the LDLR in response to sterol signaling.
the molecular mechanisms that control the uptake, trafficking, and degradation of cholesterol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LXR-IDL axis defines a clatrin-, caveol-, dynamin-independent endosomal route for LDLR endocytosis and lysosomal degradation.
IDOL-mediated LDLR ubiquityation is a sorting signal for the LDLR to be targeted to the endosome for lysosomal degradation, and that this process is independent of clatrin, caveolin and dynamin.
LXR and IDOL regulate LDLR internalization through a novel endocytic pathway that is distinct from those used for lipoproteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LXR target IDOL controls LDLR internalization through a clathrin-independent endocytic pathway that involves ubiquitylation of a raft-associated LDLR pool.
LXR activation leads to LDLR ubiquityation by IDOL and subsequent internalization of the receptor via an ESCRT-dependent pathway.
the LXR-Induced degradation of the LDL receptor is a distinct pathway from the LDL receptor-mediated uptake of lipoproteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IDOL-dependent LDLR ubiquityation is a sorting signal that targets the LDLR for degradation via the endosomal ESCRT system.
IDOL-dependent LDLR internalization is a novel clathrin-, dynamin-, caveolin-, and autophagy-independent route for LDLR endocytosis and lysosomal degradation.
LXR-IDOL-dependent LDLR degradation occurs via a novel, ESCRT- and dynamin-dependent endocytic pathway.
